root_cause.title: rotate() check-then-act race across two browser tabs: Tab B's synchronous revokeFamily() always runs before Tab A's repo.insert(), leaving Tab A's new token in a revoked family — both tabs lose their session
root_cause.explanation: When two browser tabs refresh at the same time with the same rt cookie, both call POST /auth/refresh concurrently. Inside rotate(), Tab A executes all synchronous statements through repo.revoke(row.id) at line 60, which commits the revocation to the DB, and then yields at 'await users.findById()' at line 61. Tab B then runs — it reads the same row via findByHash() and sees row.revoked_at already set (Tab A wrote it). Tab B enters the reuse-detection branch, calls revokeFamily() synchronously, and throws TokenReuseDetected; the controller clears Tab B's rt cookie and returns 401. Because Tab B's entire code path has no await, revokeFamily()'s two UPDATEs complete before Tab A ever resumes — this ordering is deterministic, not probabilistic. Tab A resumes, generates a new token, and calls repo.insert(); but the family is already marked revoked. The new token row enters the DB with revoked_at=NULL in a revoked family (the revokeFamily UPDATE only catches rows that existed at the time it ran). Tab A receives a 200 with a new access token, but that token's embedded fid points to a revoked family. authMiddleware's isFamilyRevoked(fid) check rejects it on the very next API call, leaving Tab A with a broken session. Neither tab shows an error: Tab B silently redirects to /login; Tab A's Dashboard Promise.all gets an unhandled rejection and shows a blank page.

causal_chain.what: Two browser tabs are independent JS contexts. Each fires POST /auth/refresh with the same rt httpOnly cookie. Client-side deduplication inside one tab cannot prevent this.
Tab A enters rotate(). repo.revoke(row.id) at L60 is the last synchronous write. It commits revoked_at for the token row to the DB. Tab A then yields at 'await users.findById()' at L61.

Tab B runs while Tab A is suspended. findByHash() returns the row with revoked_at now set. Tab B enters the if(row.revoked_at) branch at L56, calls revokeFamily() synchronously. Tab B's entire path has no await, so revokeFamily()'s two UPDATEs complete in full before Tab A can resume.
revokeFamily() UPDATE at line 44 is 'WHERE family_id = ? AND revoked_at IS NULL'. It runs before Tab A's insert(). Tab A's new token does not yet exist — the UPDATE misses it.
Tab A resumes and calls repo.insert(). The new token is inserted with revoked_at=NULL into a family whose token_families.revoked_at is now set. No schema constraint prevents this.
Tab B gets 401 + clearCookie('rt'). Tab A gets 200 + a new access token. But Tab A's new access token embeds fid = the revoked family_id.

Tab B: refreshSession() returns false → logout() → silent redirect to /login. Tab A: retries original API call with new token → authMiddleware isFamilyRevoked(fid) returns true → 401 → api() throws 'Request failed: 401' → Dashboard Promise.all has no .catch() → unhandled rejection, blank UI. No error message is shown in either tab.

hypotheses.statement: rotate()'s read-check-revoke-insert is not atomic. Tab B observes Tab A's intermediate write (revoked_at set, no new token yet) and triggers revokeFamily(), which runs to completion before Tab A can insert its new token.
Tab A's new token is inserted into a revoked family. isFamilyRevoked() then returns true for all subsequent requests using Tab A's new access token.
Client-side deduplication of refreshSession() (the original fix direction) prevents the race within a single tab but cannot prevent two separate browser tabs from both sending POST /auth/refresh.
hypotheses.reason: Each browser tab has its own JS heap. A shared in-flight promise in apiClient.ts is not shared across tabs. The bug is fully reproducible with two tabs regardless of any client-side fix.

hypotheses.statement: Tab A is left with a broken session (blank Dashboard, not a login redirect) because api() throws without calling logout() when the retry fails at line 40.
Users are randomly logged out simply because the access token expired with no retry path.
hypotheses.reason: A refresh path exists and functions correctly for a single tab. The failure is specific to concurrent rotation of the same token.

fix_direction.summary: A db.transaction() alone is insufficient: it serialises the sync DB calls but does not change what Tab B sees or does — Tab B still reads row.revoked_at as set, still enters the reuse branch, still calls revokeFamily(), and still throws TokenReuseDetected. The logic inside rotate() must change. The fix has two parts: (1) Replace the read-then-write claim with a single atomic UPDATE: 'UPDATE refresh_tokens SET revoked_at = ? WHERE id = ? AND revoked_at IS NULL'. Check stmt.run().changes. If changes === 1 this caller won the race; proceed to sign and insert successor. If changes === 0 someone else already claimed this token — go to step 2. (2) Distinguish concurrent race from theft by checking whether a live successor for this family was created within a short grace window (e.g. 30 seconds). If a live successor exists with created_at >= now - GRACE_MS: this is a concurrent re-submission of the same original token — issue a fresh rotation of that live successor (sign a new access token + insert a new refresh token as its child) so the caller gets a fully valid session. If no live successor exists, or the revocation is older than the grace window: it is genuine theft — call revokeFamily() and throw TokenReuseDetected as today. This requires two new repo operations: (a) an atomic claim UPDATE that returns changes count, and (b) a findLiveByFamily query that returns the current unrevoked token row for a family. All synchronous DB operations should be wrapped in db.transaction() to prevent partial writes, but the critical correctness fix is the atomic claim + grace-window distinction, not the transaction alone.
fix_direction.regression_test_idea: Three tests in demo-app/api/tests/ using Vitest + supertest at HTTP level. Setup: login alice, capture the rt cookie value. Test 1 — concurrent same-token (the bug): send 3 concurrent POST /auth/refresh requests all with the same rt cookie (Promise.all of 3 supertest calls). Assert all 3 respond with status 200. Assert all 3 bodies contain an accessToken. Assert all 3 new accessTokens pass GET /me with status 200. Assert isFamilyRevoked is false after all 3 settle. Test 2 — stale token after real rotation (theft detection must still work): send POST /auth/refresh with the original rt cookie to get a new rt2. Then send POST /auth/refresh with the original rt cookie again (simulating theft of the old token, well after rotation). Assert the second call returns 401. Assert that GET /me with rt2's accessToken now also returns 401 (family was revoked). Test 3 — normal single rotation: send POST /auth/refresh once with rt cookie, assert 200 + new accessToken + GET /me 200. Assert the original rt cookie now returns 401 on a second refresh attempt.
